title: Yaakov Matza’ah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Megillah 23a](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.23a) he asked Rav Yehuda: “To whom do these six (people called to the Torah) on Yom Kippur correspond?” In [Chullin 84a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.84a) he challenged Rava: “We hold that a wild animal is included in the category of a domesticated animal with respect to the identifying signs; say the same here too,” etc. In both places the Gemara reads “Yaakov Mina’ah,” whereas Tosafot reads “Matza’ah,” contradicting its own statement in [Avodah Zarah 17a](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosafot_on_Avodah_Zarah.17a), at the comment beginning “Ve-Yaakov.”[^1]

notes.text: The parenthetical explanation of the six readers is printed in Hyman. קימ״ל is the ordinary expression “we hold”; סימנין is rendered “identifying signs” without supplying a fuller legal argument. The readings מינאה and מצעה, and the claimed contradiction in Tosafot, are Hyman’s report and have not been independently verified. The printed folio labels כג., פד. and יז. are conventionally 23a, 84a and 17a.
